$comment: Acceptance criteria for issue 151, declared before the work and confirmed red: ADR-013 is Accepted and is absent from get_constraints today, because prose explaining supersession was read as a supersession record. Criterion 1 asserts the CONSEQUENCE -- a live Accepted decision reaching the compiled constraints -- rather than the mechanism, because the mechanism could be fixed in a way that still drops it. Criterion 2 is the negative control the mechanism needs: an ADR whose header genuinely declares supersession must still be treated as superseded, or the fix would have traded one wrong answer for the opposite one. STRENGTHENED DURING THE WORK, recorded rather than done quietly: fixture criteria were ADDED because criteria 1 and 2 depend on the real ledger -- editing ADR-013 or ADR-014 for unrelated reasons would break them and teach nobody anything. The fixture carries the exact prose that caused the defect, so the regression is reproducible without this repository's own history. Adding criteria strengthens a bar; nothing was loosened.

criteria.target: python3 -c "import subprocess,sys,json;o=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'adapters/adr','query','architecture','get_constraints','id=x'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout;v=json.loads(o).get('value') or {};sys.exit(0 if 'ADR-013' in [c['id'] for c in v.get('constraints') or []] else 1)"

python3 -c "import subprocess,sys,json;o=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'adapters/adr','query','architecture','get_superseded_decisions'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout;v=json.loads(o).get('value') or {};ids=[d['id'] for d in v.get('decisions') or []];sys.exit(0 if 'ADR-014' in ids and 'ADR-013' not in ids else 1)"
